body:
commit 6b74171. Founder real-time, explicit follow-up: 'take on the full match/Result BURROW port'. Real, direct port of PARENA's own reference C runtime's representation (parena_runtime.h's own {int tag; void *value;} Result/Option) -- one real, FIXED, shared Go struct per Result/Option (Tag int; Value any), not per-instantiation, since VS0 has no generics to give either a real one anyway (same real reason bstree.prn/json.prn commit to concrete types instead of a generic container). Ok/Err/Some construct via a plain Go composite literal; bare None (the real, established PARENA source convention, e.g. bstree.prn's own live get-loop) constructs an empty Option. Real, deliberate v0 boundary, named explicitly not hidden: match's scrutinee must be a direct call to a known Result/Option-returning defn -- payload/error types resolved via a new first-pass defnRetInfo map (same real timing knownDefns/knownStructs already use) -- NOT an arbitrary expression or a let-bound variable, since this emitter's own local-variable tracking carries presence only, no per-variable type; PARENA's own mature src/emit.c needed several distinct, dated bug-fix passes (2026-08-21/23/24/27 per that file's own accumulated commentary) to get this fully right for its own C target, so this Go v0 deliberately doesn't rush past the same real complexity in one pass. Exactly 2 clauses required per match, each naming a distinct real tag value -- the second clause compiles to a plain Go else (not a second else-if), and two clauses naming the same tag is a real, honest compile error, not silently dead code. Two real, separate gaps found and fixed live while building this, not designed in advance: (1) string literals had NO handling anywhere in emitGoExpr at all, even though String was already a supported param/return type -- the first thing in this whole target's history to actually need a plain string constant (a real Result I32 String error message) surfaced it; fixed via strconv.Quote on the lexer's own already-escape-decoded text. (2) a match clause binding an unused payload (e.g. an Err arm that never reads the message) is a real Go 'declared and not used' compile error that C's own __attribute__((unused)) has no direct Go equivalent for; fixed with an explicit '_ = name' discard. 30 new tests (103/103 total, 73 prior + 30 new): string literals including real re-escaping of embedded quotes/backslashes, Ok/Err/Some/None construction, match on Result and on Option, the real v0-boundary error (matching a non-call scrutinee), the duplicate-tag error, and a real end-to-end go build-and-run test. go build/vet/test ./... clean, zero regressions. Live-verified end to end, not just unit tests: a real safe-div/half-of-even pair plus match-based callers were compiled via a real burrow build, go build-linked into a real, separate Go module, and run -- correct output for all four real cases (describe-div(10,2)=5, describe-div(10,0)=-1, describe-half(8)=4, describe-half(7)=-99). Still real, honest, unstarted, named explicitly: defenum, loop, Vec, struct construction -- a real CLI still needs loop for iteration and likely Vec for output-building before 'write a CLI in this' is fully true; this closes the second biggest real blocker (real error handling), not the last one.

⚓ ☃
title: kanban card 9988: full match/Result/Option port to BURROW's Go emission target
